work_packages.name: On the CPU alone, rain fills the hollows of a stretch of ground: puddles stand level where it dips, spill into each other, join into one and part again as they dry, and ground under a roof stays dry
work_packages.quality_bar: Standing water a hydrologist would accept, held to brute force as Barnes's fill-spill-merge is held to a flood: every puddle level in its own hollow, and every litre accounted for through each spill, merge and parting. Nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: `thrum-rain-model` cuts a bed grid into its tree of hollows. On a bed the test makes, with three bowls, a rut, a slope and small relief: every pit is a hollow; each cell is reached from its hollow's pit by a path that never descends; each pair's sill is the lowest pass between them; a hollow shallower than the profile's least depth is filled; a hollow under four cells across is reported; and the same bed gives the same bytes.
items.ask: Read the test. Are the expected hollows, sills and paths worked out there from the bed by brute force, without the code under test?

items.statement: The point test is exact. Over 200 seeded beds and fills, the cells where a hollow's level stands above the cell's bed are the cells a flood from the pits reaches under the same levels: no cell differs, with puddles that span one hollow and several.
items.ask: Is the flood in the test written apart from the tree's code, and does it start from pits only? Would a point test that read one level for the whole body fail it?

items.statement: Puddles fill, spill, merge and part. Under steady rain a full hollow's excess goes to the hollow across its sill; two that are full to one sill become one puddle at one level; under a loss they part at the sill, each keeping its own side's water. A hollow beyond a ridge stays dry until water spills into it. In every tick, a merge's and a parting's included, a hollow's level moves by no more than the water that entered or left its puddle's hollows in that tick over the smallest water surface any of those puddles had before or after it, taken as at least one cell.
items.ask: Does the test take its bound on a level's change from the tick's own volumes and surfaces, and does it cover a merge of two puddles that are each already several hollows? Would a fill that set both levels to their mean at a merge fail it?

items.statement: The water account closes. Over 10,000 ticks with merges and partings, the rain on the body equals the change in the puddles plus what dried, went down into the ground, was withheld by canopy and left over the edge, within 1e-9 of the rain. On ground that takes nothing, a pothole with six times its area draining to it fills in a sixth of the time. A puddle with no other ground draining to it, on ground whose percolation rate is at least the rain's, does not grow.

Shelter is content. From shelters the test gives, each a set of triangles with one share of rain it lets through, exposure is 0 under a roof, the crown's share under a tree, 1 under open sky, on the roof's own top and outside the grid, and passes between them over the profile's edge width. Under a crown that stands under a roof it is 0 at the ground and between the two and 1 above the roof; under two crowns it is the product of their shares; a shelter counts once in a column however many of its triangles cross it; and a column three shelters cross is refused by name and place. A hollow under a roof fills only by what drains to it from open ground, and one with no open ground stays dry.
items.ask: Would exposure taken from the lowest canopy alone fail the crown under the roof, as part 10 of `docs/evidence/PUDDLES/design-proof/revision_proof.py` shows?

items.statement: Each tick's rain on a cell goes to one receiver, the first thing it hits, and each receiver's gain is right alone. On a bed the test makes, with a puddle covering part of its hollow, a roof's edge over part of the water and a crown over part of the ground: the canopy's sink gains what each layer withholds over the cells it covers; the puddle gains the rain on its own water surface, by the exposure there; the runoff is the rain on the uncovered ground that drains to it; and the edge's sink takes the rest. Each entry of the account is the test's own sum over cells for that receiver, within 1e-9, at three fills.
items.ask: Does the test sum each receiver's cells by brute force from the bed, the levels and the shelters, without the model? Does it check each entry by itself and not only their sum?
items.evidence: crates/thrum-rain-model/tests/receivers.rs: passed on 2ae13f69c4bf3577424ca00035eaf230482f1010 (mac-metal), and fails on the code before the fix; .orchestrate/evidence/PUDDLES/WP1-evidence.md

items.statement: Ruling 1 is built on the CPU: `thrum-water-model`'s map takes a hollows body (a rectangle, its own bed, a label for each cell, a level for each hollow) and gives the body, level, bed and depth at any point by the point test, with no current and no wind gain. Its identity and generation are the same before and after its puddles merge. Refused by name: a hollows body with a cell in another body's water or shore margin anywhere in that body's stage range, and one over the profile's count of cells or hollows. A table that stands two levels in wet cells that touch is held at the last table and counted.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model --test map && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Is the change to the map confined to the new kind, so that no body an existing test or the example declares is prepared or answered differently? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` changed?

items.statement: The rain state is plain data a game keeps in its world. It encodes and decodes to the same bytes, and stepping it from the same state and inputs gives the same bytes on one thread and on eight.

`WATERS`' conformance model answers on a hollows body: a point in a puddle gives the body and its depth, a point on dry ground between two puddles gives dry, and the answers either side of a merge differ only by the level's change.

`scripts/rain_cost.py` records, on this Mac in a release build, the preparation of a bed of 640,000 cells (seconds, hollows, nodes, bytes) and a fill step with every hollow holding water, with the commit and the load on the machine. `check` fails only when either cannot be measured or the committed record lacks a field.
items.ask: Was the record taken on this work package's code, in a release build, and does it give the bytes a node's curve of level for volume takes?

items.statement: `thrum-rain-model` builds and its tests run with no graphics device and no dependency on `thrum-render` or `wgpu`, it is registered in `.config/architecture.toml`, and it holds no island, yard, preset or ground table.

work_packages.name: On the CPU alone, ground wets and dries as ground does, sheen first and darkness last, and a raindrop's rings spread as water's own waves do
work_packages.quality_bar: Wet ground and rain rings a physics text would accept: two stores that keep their water through a shower long enough to fill the pores, darkening that follows from the film's optics, and rings that follow from water's dispersion and outlive the rain that made them, each held to the test's own arithmetic as parts 3 to 5 and 8 to 10 of the design proofs hold them.

items.statement: The ground's two stores step with the tick for each ground class, in the open and where a half and a quarter of the rain reaches. Through a shower on paving the pores fill at the soak rate, then surface water stands up to what the relief holds and the rest is runoff; after it the surface water goes at the drying rate and the pores' fill falls only once it has gone. On earth with 3 mm of pores, a soak rate of 15 mm/h, 0.5 mm of relief and a percolation rate of 5 mm/h, under 10 mm/h with drying off: no surface water stands for the 1,080 s the pores take to fill, a film stands from then, and the relief is full and runoff starts at 1,440 s, each within two ticks. Ground whose soak rate and percolation rate are both at least the rain's takes no surface water through two hours of it; ground that percolates 15 mm/h and soaks 5 takes a film under 10 mm/h while its pores fill. With the stores, the marks' transfers and the pores under the marks in it, WP1.4's account still closes within 1e-9, with rain its only source.
items.ask: Are the expected times and fills worked out in the test from the rates, as parts 5 and 8 of the design proofs do, and not read from the model? Does the shower run on past the time the pores fill?

items.statement: The wetness function gives the pores' fill and the surface water with its cover at a world point, from prepared fields and the rain state alone. It reads the stores by exposure, and is nothing under a roof; a wall takes a quarter of the ground's and an underside none; relief on a slope holds less, down to none at the class's steepest slope; where a class has a pattern, surface water covers its lows first. On the paving and the earth of part 5 of the design proof, ground that 0.4 of the rain reaches differs from that ground stepped by itself by no more than 0.3 of the pores and 0.15 mm of surface water.

A hollow's margin follows the design's rule: each tick a fall of the level adds to it, a rise takes from it down to nothing, and it then shrinks by `exp(-dt * drying rate / pore capacity)` and stays under the hollow's rim. Under a steady fall, where a tick is under 0.02 of the pore capacity over the drying rate and the band stays under the rim, it settles within 2% at the fall's rate times the pore capacity over the drying rate, so a slow fall leaves a thin band and a fast one a wide band; a rise takes its own height from the band, so one at least as high as the band leaves none and a smaller one leaves the rest; when the level stops falling the band halves in `ln 2` times the capacity over the drying rate; with drying at nothing it stays; and a hollow that has emptied keeps its band until it has faded. Inside a body's wave support the pores are full, and above it they fall off over that body's margin, kept by the same rule from its stage. A margin and a shore's band add no water to the account.
items.ask: Does the shore's case read the wave support from `thrum-water-model`'s own function, so that it is the support `WATERS`' film reads?

items.statement: The wet look's reference darkens a base colour channel by channel by `(1 - R)(1 - p) a / (1 - p a)`, mixed in by the pores' fill times porosity: 0.55 of an albedo of 0.1 and 0.83 of 0.8 at `p` = 0.47, within 0.01; a brown's saturation rises; a metal is unchanged; a material with no porosity of its own takes the rule on roughness and metalness.

A drop's rings follow from water's dispersion with surface tension, depth and viscosity. The least group speed is 17.8 cm/s within 0.3. For a 3 mm drop over a crater three drop radii across, the rings' energy is the closed form's for a Gaussian impulse on deep water within 2%, and between 0.8% and 1.4% of the drop's; 0.8 s after, the highest ring is 0.14 mm within a fifth and the water within 11 cm of the drop's place stands under a tenth of that; and the height on 5 mm, 2 mm and 1 mm of water over the height on deep water is 0.76, 0.41 and 0.25 within 0.05.
items.ask: Does the test integrate the response itself, with its own Bessel function, and take the energy's closed form from its own algebra?

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the CPU: `thrum-water-model`'s surface model sums two rain bands through the one sum, with the depth limit and moments a wave layer has. The bands are a function of time and of the committed rate history: the same time and history give the same field whatever was evaluated before. A drop is born by the rate at its own tick. Through rain that runs, stops and starts again 0.6 s later, each ring born before the stop is in the field through the rest of its second at the height the table gives, no ring is born at a tick with no rain, no ring at the restart has a birth in the dry spell, and a second after a stop with no restart the field is exactly nothing. Scheduled rings over a patch follow the rain rate up to the profile's count, and the drops below the cut add their squared slope to the moments by the same history. The gain at a point is exposure times the depth response, on every body, the sea included, and none under a roof. With no rain bands every answer of the model is the same to the bit.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model --test rain_bands && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Do the bands hold any state between evaluations other than the committed history, or any power that depends on the wind? Would births read from the present rate fail the stop and the restart, as part 9 of `docs/evidence/PUDDLES/design-proof/revision_proof.py` shows? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` changed?

items.statement: With the stores in, each tick's rain on a cell still goes to the first thing it hits, found from the bed, the shelters and the puddle's level at the tick's start, and never from a mark: the puddle where its water stands, by the exposure at the water's surface; held ground where a mark stands above the water, by the exposure at the ground; and open ground elsewhere, whose stores are those of open ground stepped by itself. Held ground's rain meets its share, by area, of the pores under the mark: they take it at the soak rate while the share has room and then only at the percolation rate, which goes down, and the rest is runoff to the puddle. On a dish that holds ground over full pores, part 11d's, when rain starts again at 1 mm/h, under its class's 5 mm/h percolation rate, the puddle gains from the rain only what falls on its water and all of the held ground's rain goes down; at 100 mm/h the held ground passes 5 mm/h down and the rest runs to the puddle; and on a floor that holds ground with room in its pores, half under a crown, the pores gain the held ground's rain. Each receiver's gain, with the held ground's three parts, is the test's own sum over cells within 1e-9, apart from the total WP2.1 closes.
items.ask: Does the test sum each receiver's cells from the bed, the shelters and the level at the tick's start, reading the mark only to tell held ground from open ground? Would a model that gave the puddle the rain on held ground fail it, at the rain under the percolation rate, though that model's total closes? Would one that passed a puddle's rain through the ground's stores?

items.statement: A hollow's mark moves by the design's rule, and no water is made or owed. Where the level rises over ground, that ground's surface water joins the puddle and its pore water joins the pores under the mark. Where it falls, the ground it leaves takes its class's state: its pore water comes from its share of the pores under the mark, what the share holds beyond the class's fill is counted as soaked, and what it lacks comes from the puddle with the class's surface water. A hollow whose puddle holds less than that keeps the ground: nothing moves, the wetness function gives that ground the fill of the pores under the mark with the margin's band and no surface water, and all of it is handed over on the first tick the puddle can pay. On a level floor of 8 by 8 cells in a 4 cm rim with 3 mm of pores, at soak rates of 1 and 30 mm/h, relief of 0.1 and 3 mm and showers of 50, 150 and 500 s at 60 mm/h, each with three hours of drying at 20 mm/h; on a hollow that holds ground for more than one tick, with rain falling on it while it is held; and on two hollows that share a puddle through a merge and a parting: each entry is the test's own figure within 1e-9, no entry is more than its donor held before it, and the account closes on rain alone.
items.ask: Does the test take each donor's water from the state before the entry, and check that the donor lost what the receiver gained? Does the held case show ground kept for more than one tick and then handed over? Does the rain state keep any quantity that stands for water not yet delivered?

items.statement: The bed under a puddle takes water as open ground's pores take rain. While the pores under the mark have room it takes the class's soak rate over the water's surface, and the pores gain what they have room for; over full pores, and on ground with none, it takes the percolation rate, on a class that soaks 15 mm/h and percolates 5 and on one that soaks 1 and percolates 15; and a puddle that holds less than a tick's drying and take gives each its share of what it holds and is empty. From dry, on a level floor with 3 mm of pores that soak 1 mm/h and 0.1 mm of relief, under 60 mm/h, the puddle that stands gains each tick the rain on it and the runoff to it, less 1 mm/h over its surface. Each entry, and the change in the puddle and in the pores under the mark, is the test's own figure within 1e-9.
items.ask: Does the test work each figure from the cells, the stores and the puddle's water at the tick's start, without the model? Would a model that filled the pores under a puddle at once fail it, and one that took the lesser of the two rates over full pores?

work_packages.name: On the island, rain fills the hollows of a yard: puddles lie level in the ground, grow, join and shrink with a clean waterline, show the ground through them and mirror the sky, and a float sits in one
work_packages.quality_bar: Puddles as on the streets of The Last of Us Part II's Seattle and the trails of Red Dead Redemption 2 after rain: water lying level in the ground's own dips, a clean waterline that follows the ground, the ground seen through clear shallows and lost under muddy water, with no stair of cells, sliver, curtain or pop.

items.statement: Ruling 6 is built for `examples/water`: a rain selection, off by default. With it off the island's ground, bodies, tick page and compiled graph are what they were. With it on the island has a yard by the lake, with paving that dips, a track of packed earth with ruts, a roof on posts, a wall and a post standing in a pothole 15 cm deep, as a hollows body with its ground classes, and the game keeps a rain state in its world and steps it.
items.ask: With the selection off, does any code path of the game or of `thrum-water` differ from before this work package? Is the yard's ground reached only with the selection on?

items.statement: `WATERS`' own body and stage tests pass unchanged with the selection off.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --test bodies_gpu && cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --test stage_gpu

items.statement: Ruling 1 is built on the GPU. For a bed the test makes, at five fills that include the ticks before and after a merge, the body, level, bed and depth the GPU's map gives at 4,096 scattered points and along every puddle's waterline are `thrum-water-model`'s, at the tolerance `WATERS` WP4.1's test states. A scene with no hollows body compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before this work package.
items.ask: Is a hollows body reached only through declarations any game can make, with no path in `thrum-water` that knows the island? Does the test fail when the GPU reads one level for the whole body?

items.statement: Each puddle is drawn level and whole. Seen from above, each pixel's water or ground is what the CPU model gives for that place, except within a cell of a waterline; the depth the water writes over each puddle is its level at the tolerance `WATERS` WP4.1's test states; and no triangle of the surface joins two levels over water.

A merge and a parting rebuild and reset nothing. Through both, the water creates no pipeline or resource, its history is marked invalid no more often than `WATERS`' reset rule gives, the body's identity and generation hold, and a float's query answers follow the level with no step.
A float released in a puddle sits at its level and rises as it fills; a query on the dry ground beside it and under the roof answers dry.

The puddles read as water lying in the ground: each level, meeting the paving and the earth in a clean line that follows the ground, with no stair of cells, no sliver on dry ground and no edge hanging in the air. The paving shows through its shallow puddles and the track's puddles are muddy and hide their bed. The sky lies in them. The film and the wet ground are not built until WP5 and are not judged here.

work_packages.name: Rain rings every water it falls on, the puddles, the lake and the sea, more and rougher as it grows and not at all under the roof, and the rings run out when the rain stops
work_packages.quality_bar: Rain on water as on the lakes of Red Dead Redemption 2 and the street puddles of The Last of Us Part II, and past both in that each ring is the water's own wave: it starts small and sharp, spreads leaving calm water inside it, gains crests and fades, with no grid, repeat or stamped circle.

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the GPU. The two rain bands, evaluated at the display's time, agree with `thrum-water-model`'s at three times, one of them 0.4 s after the rain stops, at a tolerance the test states, which bands evaluated half a tick late and bands that ignore the rate history both miss. A repeated frame at one time draws the same bands, and a capture at a tick draws that tick's, from its history. A scene without the capability compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before.
items.ask: Do the bands keep any texture from one frame to the next?

items.statement: The bands' gain is the model's. Under the roof the drawn surface carries no ring and in the open it carries them; a ring on 2 mm of water is the depth response's share of one on a deep puddle; the lake and the sea carry them; and the rings counted over a patch follow the rain at 2, 10 and 50 mm/h. The passes run while any tick of the last second held rain and not after: 0.4 s after the rain stops the surface still carries the rings born before it, and from a second after it the passes do not run and the surface is what it is with no rain.

From 0.5 m and from 1.7 m the rings read as rain on water: each starts small and sharp, spreads leaving calm water inside it, gains crests and fades. Light rain is a few rings, heavy rain a crowded, roughened surface. No grid, repeat or pair of like rings shows across a puddle 6 m long. Under the roof's edge the rings stop along a soft line, and on the thinnest water they are faint.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the yard's largest puddle from 0.5 m and 1.7 m at 2, 10 and 50 mm/h, one framed on the roof's edge and one on a puddle's shallow margin; `fixed` stills cropped at native size of single rings at three ages.

items.statement: From a distance rained-on water dulls and its reflections soften, more as the rain grows, on the lake and the sea as on the puddles, with no line where the rings end and no shimmer.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences from 30 m above the lake and from the beach looking out to sea, at no rain, 10 and 50 mm/h, in a calm and in a breeze.

items.statement: Stopping the rain reads as rain stopping: the rings on the water spread out and fade over a second and no new one starts, the water does not snap to still, and when the rain starts again the first rings are small and new.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the yard's largest puddle from 0.5 m and 1.7 m at 10 and 50 mm/h through a stop, two seconds of no rain and a restart; consecutive frames across the stop and across the restart at native size.

items.statement: The rain bands' cadence is a named runtime value in `EFFECT-GRAPH`'s list with a declared invalidation. Lowering it changes no query answer.
In Chrome rain rings the puddles and the lake and not the water under the roof, and the rings run out after the rain is stopped.

The paired cost record for rain at 50 mm/h on the yard and the lake is taken again at 2560x1440, beside WP3's. It also holds two CPU times. One is labelling regions as the puddles fill. The other is the game's tick draining ready answers from the query mailbox for the example's craft and eight floats, 54 stations at their own radii: the median and the longest drain of at least 60 ticks in that rain, and of the same batch with no rain. A drain in the rain longer than a tenth of the tick trips a wire. Each wire the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.

The rain's share of a query answer is the bands' own function over the station's disc, at the tick the answer is used at. In f64, at footprint radii of 0.04 m, 0.128 m and 0.278 m, the model's footprint read agrees with a direct average of the bands over the disc in height, both slopes and rate, at a tolerance the test states, which a read at a point and the patch's mean both miss at 0.04 m. From a radius of 0.64 m the read is the patch's mean, with no slope. The mailbox's answers at 0.128 m and 0.278 m, the radii of the example's floats and craft, are the model's read for the use tick.

findings.name: Rain footprint evaluation stalls the simulation tick
Rain query slopes omit the spatial derivative of carriage
findings.different: The repaired query samples the correct departure and carries height rate. On a spatially varying track its slope still lacks the departure and blend gradients needed for a world-space answer.

work_packages.name: A footfall or a dropped stone in a puddle sends rings across it at the speed its depth gives, and they die at its edge and stop at a dry sill
work_packages.quality_bar: Rings from a step in a puddle as on the street puddles of The Last of Us Part II, and past them in that each ring is the water's own wave: round, crossing at the speed the depth gives and slower in the shallower puddle, dying at the edge, and stopped exactly by a dry sill.

items.statement: Ruling 2 is built on the GPU. On the fine level a footfall's rings cross 30 mm of water faster than 10 mm and never grow, and a frame more than two ticks ahead takes two steps and counts the rest as dropped. A ring raised in one puddle leaves the next exactly at rest across a dry sill and crosses it once the two have merged, with the height and potential the level held before the merge still in it. `WATERS`' interaction tests pass unchanged with the fine level in the profile and without it.

items.statement: With the fine level in the profile, a source's waves are split between the interaction levels and each is counted once: outside the 1 m crossing a wave is on one level alone. A stone's impulse inside the fine window raises a wave both grids can hold, such as one 0.64 m long, on the fine level, and the near level's state stays at rest in it. A wave a few metres long from the same impulse is on the near level and not on the fine one. The same impulse with no fine level in the profile puts the 0.64 m wave on the near level, as `WATERS` built it.

work_packages.name: The ground itself gets wet: paving and earth darken as the rain starts, a sheen gathers in the paving's joints and mirrors what stands on it, the ground under the roof stays dry, sand is dark where waves have run, and it dries sheen first and darkness last
work_packages.quality_bar: Wet ground as on the streets of The Last of Us Part II's Seattle and in Red Dead Redemption 2's Saint Denis: deeper, darker colour where the ground drinks, a sheen where it cannot, reflections at a grazing view, a dry floor under every roof, and drying that goes in the order real ground dries, with no tint laid over the scene and nothing that pops.

items.statement: Ruling 5 is built. With a wetness provider registered, the scene's shader and the cooked material read the wetness function before a surface is lit. With none, the scene's shader text, pipelines and storage are what they were. With one and a dry rain state, every submitted pixel of the example and of the V1 game's default scene is what it was with none.

items.statement: As a shower starts the paving and the earth darken and their colour deepens, the earth more than the pale paving. On the paving a sheen gathers in the joints first and then across the slabs, and at a grazing view it mirrors the post, the wall and the roof's edge. The earth darkens at once and takes no sheen while its pores fill; once they are full a sheen stands in its ruts, after the paving's. The ground under the roof stays dry to a soft edge, the roof's top is wet, rocks and the wall darken, the wall less than the ground, and metal does not.

items.statement: After the rain it dries in order: the sheen goes first, from the slope before the level slabs and from the slabs' faces before their joints; the darkness lingers and lifts last; and each shrinking puddle leaves a dark margin that fades. Nothing pops, and no edge of a cell or a texture's tile shows.
